subject: microbiology
title: Obligate Anaerobes and Microscopy: Dark Ground, Phase Contrast and Electron Methods

steps.tx: **Obligate anaerobes** are poisoned by oxygen because they lack or scant superoxide dismutase and catalase, letting superoxide and hydrogen peroxide accumulate fatally; aerotolerant species (many clostridia, lactobacilli) endure oxygen without using it. The roster that matters clinically: Clostridium, Bacteroides and Prevotella, Fusobacterium, Peptostreptococcus and Actinomyces, dominating abscesses below the diaphragm and wherever tissue dies.
steps.say: Oxygen is a poison these bacteria cannot detoxify; dead tissue is their invitation.

left.title: Oxygen defence ladder
points: Obligate aerobes: full SOD and catalase
Obligate anaerobes: defences absent, oxygen lethal

right.title: Clinical roster
points: Actinomyces: chronic lumpy jaw and IUD infections

steps.tx: **Anaerobic culture is** an engineering discipline: specimens in anaerobic transport media (never refrigerated swabs drying in air), Robertson cooked meat and thioglycollate broths, anaerobic jars with GasPak hydrogen and catalyst or McIntosh Fildes evacuation, indicator methylene blue staying colourless, and prereduced media in cabinets for the fastidious. A pus Gram stain showing bacteria that refuse aerobic culture is anaerobes announcing a transport failure, not their absence.
steps.say: No growth aerobically from foul pus means the transport failed the anaerobes, not that pus was sterile.

nodes.label: Aspirate or tissue into anaerobic transport medium
Plated on blood agar, incubated anaerobically

steps.tx: **Dark ground microscopy** makes the invisible luminous: a special condenser illuminates obliquely so only light scattered by organisms reaches the eye, showing living thin spirochaetes (Treponema pallidum in chancre fluid) bright on black, unstained and motile. It remains the immediate test of early syphilis where serology still sleeps, with oral commensal treponemes as its specificity trap in mouth lesions.
steps.say: Spirochaetes too thin to stain shine in dark ground; use it on genital chancres, not mouths.

left.title: Dark ground facts
points: Detects motile T pallidum in primary chancre

right.title: Microscopy family
points: Phase contrast: living unstained cells by phase shifts
Bright field with stains: routine bench

steps.tx: **Dark ground microscopy** is how Treponema pallidum is seen while it is still alive. A condenser sends light in at a slant, the direct beam misses the lens, and only light scattered by the thin spiral reaches the eye, so the organism shines on a black field. Fluid from a genital chancre is the specimen that counts. The mouth is a trap, because ordinary oral spirochaetes look much the same. A positive field from a chancre supports primary syphilis before the blood test has become reactive.
steps.say: Dark ground microscopy shows living Treponema pallidum as a bright spiral on a black field, and the specimen should come from a genital chancre rather than the mouth.

vis.alt: Dark ground microscopy field of Treponema pallidum as a bright spiral on black
vis.caption: A dark ground field shows Treponema pallidum as a thin bright spiral moving on a black background. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Phase contrast** converts invisible phase shifts through transparent living cells into brightness, letting laboratories watch motility, spores and cell division without killing the specimen, while fluorescence microscopy (auramine for acid fast screening, fluorescein tagged antibodies for direct antigen detection) trades natural contrast for labelled specificity. Each method answers a different specimen question, which is why the microscope bench keeps all three.
steps.say: Phase shows living structure, fluorescence shows labelled identity, dark ground shows the unstainable.

left.title: Phase contrast uses
points: Wet mounts: motility and morphology alive

steps.tx: **Electron microscopy resolves** what light cannot: transmission EM shows viral morphology (rotavirus wheels, poxvirus bricks, coronavirus crowns that named an era), internal bacterial ultrastructure and immune EM aggregation, while scanning EM renders surfaces (biofilms on catheters) in three dimensional theatre. Negative staining with phosphotungstate made stool virus diagnosis possible before molecular methods inherited the work.
steps.say: EM named viruses by silhouette for decades; PCR inherited the diagnosis, not the portraits.

left.title: Transmission EM
points: Negative stain viral morphology in stool and vesicles

right.title: Scanning EM
points: Surface topography of cells and biofilms

steps.tx: **Electron microscopy** shows what light cannot resolve. Transmission images display viral shape, including rotavirus wheels, poxvirus bricks, and the coronavirus crowns that later named a pandemic era. The same method reveals internal bacterial ultrastructure and can aggregate particles with specific antibody in immune electron microscopy. Scanning electron microscopy instead renders surfaces, such as biofilms on catheters, as three dimensional relief. Negative staining with phosphotungstate once allowed viruses in stool to be recognised by outline, before molecular tests took over diagnosis while the portraits remained.
steps.say: Transmission electron microscopy draws viruses by shape: rotavirus wheels, poxvirus bricks, and coronavirus crowns. It also shows bacterial interiors and antibody clumped particles. Scanning microscopy maps surfaces such as catheter biofilms. Phosphotungstate negative stain once diagnosed stool viruses from their silhouettes. PCR later took the diagnostic role, not the portraits.

vis.alt: A transmission electron micrograph shows virus particles with distinctive outlines such as wheels, bricks, or crowns.
vis.caption: Transmission electron microscopy renders viral silhouettes, including wheel like rotavirus, poxvirus bricks, and crowned coronavirus particles. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Anaerobic infection signatures** teach recognition before culture returns: foul smelling pus, gas in tissues, black discharge, sulphur granules (Actinomyces), infections hugging mucosal surfaces (below diaphragm, oral, pelvic), failure of aminoglycosides (oxygen dependent uptake from the pharmacology lessons) and polymicrobial Gram stains. Metronidazole's anaerobic spectrum exists precisely for this roster.
steps.say: Foul smell, gas and mucosal neighbourhood: prescribe for anaerobes before the jar opens.

left.title: Clinical signatures
points: Putrid odour and gas in tissue
Gram stain mixed, culture aerobic silent

right.title: Therapy logic
points: Beta lactamase shields in B fragilis covered

steps.tx: **Microscope maintenance of** diagnostic value needs magnification literacy: oil immersion at 1000 fold total for bacteria, low power scanning for fluorescence sputum screens and tissue parasites, wet mount powers for ova and motility, and the discipline that morphology without specimen quality misleads (squamous cells marking sputum as saliva). The microscope rewards those who grade the specimen before naming the organism.
steps.say: Grade the specimen first; a beautiful organism in saliva is still saliva.

left.title: Magnification map
points: 100x oil: bacteria and acid fast bacilli
Fluorescence low power: rapid sputum screening

right.title: Quality gates
points: Thick and thin films divide malaria tasks
Repeat sampling beats single negative microscopy

steps.tx: **Anaerobe identification finishes** with aerotolerance testing (growth in air separates facultative impostors), spot tests (B fragilis bile tolerance and catalase), gas liquid chromatography heritage, and MALDI TOF and 16S sequencing from the culture module increasingly naming what jars only grew. The physiology lesson ends where identification begins: oxygen class is the first line of every anaerobe report.
steps.say: An anaerobe report begins with oxygen class and ends, increasingly, with a mass spectrum.
